title: MCP Toolbox for Databases -- T1548 protocol-version downgrade scope-enforcement bypass
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-11719 (fixed via
googleapis/mcp-toolbox PRs #3049 and #3335), an authenticated
authorization-bypass vulnerability in Google's MCP Toolbox for Databases.

Only the newest protocol version handler (2025-11-25) correctly enforced
per-tool `scopesRequired` restrictions. Three older, still-supported
protocol version handlers (2025-06-18, 2025-03-26, and 2024-11-05) omitted
that check entirely. An authenticated client holding only a low-privilege
token (e.g. `read`) could reach a high-privilege tool (e.g. `admin`) by
simply declaring one of the older versions in the `MCP-Protocol-Version`
HTTP header -- or by omitting the header entirely, which the server
defaults to the vulnerable 2024-11-05 handler rather than the current,
enforcing one. The vulnerability is a version-selection trapdoor, not a
broken JWT/token check: the caller's credentials are genuinely
authenticated throughout, only the SCOPE they should be limited to is
what the older handlers forgot to verify.

Detection logic flags an authenticated MCP request whose
`MCP-Protocol-Version` header is either absent or set to one of the three
vulnerable legacy values, invoking a tool name that matches this
deployment's own configured admin/high-privilege tool set -- the
header value plus tool-name pairing is the discriminator, since either
alone (an old header on a read-only tool, or an admin-tool call with the
current header) is unremarkable.

Mapped to the T1548 parent technique (Abuse Elevation Control Mechanism)
rather than a sub-technique: none of the existing sub-techniques
(sudo/sudo-caching, bypass user account control, elevated execution with
prompt, temporary elevated cloud access, TCC manipulation) describes "an
application-layer protocol-version selector that silently disables its
own newest authorization check", so this rule does not force a fit that
is not there.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor disclosure (Google/googleapis, via
the merged fix PRs), fixed in v1.3.0 (2026-05-21) and a follow-up field-
shadowing correction (PR #3335).
